newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish leftist parties bid to unseat coalition.
newsitem.headline: Turkish leftist parties bid to unseat coalition.

text.p: Turkey's two leading leftist parties said on Wednesday that they had filed censure motions against the Islamist-led government to safeguard the country's secular system.
"We handed it to the speaker of parliament at 11 o'clock (2100 GMT) last night," a spokesman for the Democratic Left Party (DSP) told Reuters.
The Republican People's Party (CHP) announced that it had filed its own censure motion early on Wednesday afternoon.
Under parliamentary rules, debate and vote on the censure motion must be held 16-23 days from the date of filing.
"Turkey's democratic and secular republic is being exposed to a serious threat and dangerous environment in the hands of this regime," the DSP statement to the speaker of parliament said.
The statement said the ruling Islamist Welfare Party was "closing its eyes to violations of the constitutional state".

Turkey's secularists have been enraged by an anti-Israel rally in an Ankara district held by the Welfare Party last week. In an apparent show of strength by the secular army, a convoy of tanks and military vehicles paraded through the area on Tuesday.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's governing coalition has a narrow majority in the 550-seat parliament in which the conservative Motherland Party is the biggest opposition party. DSP has 73 deputies and CHP has 49.

"The government is increasingly putting the primacy of the law to one side, and their efforts at putting religion first have become more apparent," Esref Erdem, a CHP spokesman, was quoted as saying by Anatolian news agency.
DSP leader Bulent Ecevit said the censure motion would be supported by many members of the junior coalition partner, the conservative True Path Party (DYP).
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, apparently renounced his radical pro-Islam and anti-Western election pledges after taking office last June.
But he has angered members of Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's DYP and the powerful army in recent weeks with plans to build mosques and other Islamist programmes.
